title: {brand} — the Claude Code sandbox runtime
description: An always-on cloud runtime for Claude Code and Codex: every session runs isolated in its own git worktree on a managed machine, keeps going when your laptop closes, and lands its work as a pull request.
h1: Every Claude Code session, in a sandbox of its own.
lede: {brand} runs Claude Code and Codex on managed machines in the cloud. Each task gets its own session in its own git worktree, keeps going when you close your laptop, and comes back as a pull request.
fine: Limited access: by invitation or request. Sessions run the official Claude Code and Codex CLIs.
term_label: Sample task list: four sessions, each in its own worktree, one waiting for an answer, one merged
term_note: laptop closed overnight... the same sessions, still there
term_cap: Sample data. The same list is in the web console and on your phone.
f_h: A runtime, not a chat window
f_sub: Your sessions live on machines that stay up, so you can hand off the work and walk away.
f1_p: Each task gets its own session and, when it names a repository, its own git worktree and branch. Uncommitted changes never mix between sessions.
f2_p: Sessions run on managed machines, not on your computer. Close the lid or go offline: they keep working. Reattach any time and the conversation is where you left it.
f3_p: Open the web console, run fleet in a terminal, or connect from a phone. Every device sees the same sessions, and the one waiting for you is listed first.
f4_p: A session working in a repository opens its own pull request and merges it only when CI is green. GitHub hosts the code and the PRs; nothing claims or closes your issues.
f5_p: Claude and ChatGPT (Codex) subscriptions form one pool behind a credential proxy; when one is full, the next request goes to another. Each person has a limit of their own, and a session never holds the subscription credential.
f6_p: Sign in with GitHub. A hosted hub is your team's own: admins invite colleagues by GitHub username, add subscriptions (ours, your own, or both) and decide who may use which.
s_h: From sign-in to a merged PR
s1_p: Invited? You are in. Not yet? Request access and we will get back to you.
s2_p: In the web console, in fleet, or from your phone. The hub records the task and opens a session in a fresh worktree.
s3_p: The session works, asks when it needs you, opens a PR and merges it on a green gate. You are told when it is done.
end_h: Put Claude Code somewhere that never sleeps.
end_p: Sign in with GitHub, or request access for your team.
